series.description: Every Gym Leader brings six. The level limits are the ones the Standard rules use.

routes_why: Route trainers (Routes 1-8 and Victory Road's ten, every record with modes.challenge whose seat tools/route_trainers.py places) get <id>_challenge too, but NOT a second entity: one trainer stands at each seat, and the trainers cycle swaps its TrainerId to the Challenge id while the nearest player within its reach carries the mode tag, and back otherwise, never during a battle (RCT_PER_PLAYER_MODE.md section 5 option R-b). That swap is ASSUMED to work (experiment E7 in that document): a data merge of TrainerId reloads the entity through readAdditionalSaveData -> setTrainerId, which was read from source, not run. If it does not work, a Challenge player meets the Normal team on routes; nothing else breaks. The Normal ids stay seriesless as before; each Challenge id is in series cobblers_challenge, optional, with no requiredDefeats, so neither moves a level cap (section 3). The mansion guardians, the HQ tower's seven and the arena's records carry no modes and get no Challenge id.
owner_decision: DECIDED by the owner on 2026-10-07 (docs/STATE.md 'What is decided', the owner's answers item 6; docs/HANDOVER_SESSION.md section 2b item 6): ONE leader per gym. All thirteen bosses stand as one person: the Normal spawner stays, the second (Challenge) spawner goes, and the trainers cycle swaps the spawner's TrainerIds and the standing trainer's TrainerId to <id>_challenge while the nearest player within reach carries the mode tag, back otherwise, never during a battle. Order: proven on Brock in staging first, then the other twelve, by widening single_leader.rollout. Until a boss is in the rollout it keeps the earlier build: both leaders, the Challenge one on bosses[].spawner.at.

single_leader.rollout_why: A list of bosses ids, or "all". Brock only until the staging proof in docs/mechanics/ONE_LEADER_SWAP.md passes (the owner's order). A boss here gets no place_<id>_challenge function and no place line; the cycle's swap drives its one spawner (data/gym_buildings leader.spawner, data/gym_interiors.json expect_spawner_at, or single_leader.normal_at for the League, which no other record carries), and reapply step R17L runs cobblers:trainers/challenge/retire_<id>_challenge once to remove the second spawner a world already holds at bosses[].spawner.at, which therefore stays recorded. A template boss (Misty, the League) also needs single_leader.restore {floor, under}: what its second spawner and redstone block replaced, measured from the template; a gym_buildings boss reads them from its own gym model.
single_leader.reach_why: rctmod-server.toml forceBattleMaxDistance (16.0) + 1, computed by tools/challenge_mode.py reach(): the farthest a trainer starts a battle on sight, so within it the leader already carries the nearest player's mode, and beyond it no battle can start.

power_kit.why: what the services decision obliges (data/training_services.json price_rule): the EV service now costs more than the hour of play it saves, so a Challenge player, who plays with no Minecraft by the owner's design, trains EVs by battle at a training ground with a power item held. The six are durable and serve every spread on every Pokemon; priced at the Mart's training shelf (data/traders.json stock_policy.mart.training tier 1, gym 2's town). Raises are NOT added: the Challenge income covers six raises a leg at every badge (SERVICES_AND_CRAFTING.md section 5). Neither are the IV service nor the vitamins: optional power, and no boss team carries EVs or IVs ("evs" occurs 0 times in data/trainers.json)

shape.rule: Oak's grant is computed.oak_cash. The rest is shared over the eight gym-clear grants in inverse proportion to the measured Challenge income of the leg each grant opens (data/markets.json income_basis.challenge.leg_by_badge for gyms 1-7; Victory Road + the League, income_basis.post_badge_8.challenge, for gym 8): the poorest leg gets the most
shape.round_to_why: each grant a multiple of $50; the rounding remainder goes to the gym-1 grant so the total is exact

voucher.delivery: a grant pays the next unpaid kits in materials first, whole kits only, then the rest in cash. Cash cannot buy back a material (no seller sells raw ore, diamonds or scrap: rule B1), so a kit must ride on a grant no later than the gym before the one it answers; the tool fails if one would not. A player may sell any material to the bank at the price it was valued at, so materials are the more flexible form

computed.oak_cash_bar: the cheapest income_gate line on any counter is $4100 (data/markets.json); Oak's cash is the largest multiple of $100 strictly below it
